company.name: Doorbot
company.one_liner: A Wi-Fi video doorbell that lets you answer your front door from your phone.

facts.summary: A battery-powered doorbell with a camera that connects to home Wi-Fi so you can see and talk to visitors from a smartphone app anywhere.
highlights: When someone rings, your phone rings and you can see and speak to them in real time.
It installs in minutes with no wiring and works with your existing doorbell chime.
It is already on sale direct-to-consumer and the company has early revenue.
It's a hardware business: inventory, manufacturing and returns all need capital.

real_deal.summary: No deal. Kevin O'Leary offered a loan plus royalty and equity; the founder declined. Every other Shark was out.

outcome.headline: Rebranded as Ring and acquired by Amazon for over $1 billion.
outcome.story: Doorbot became Ring, raised large venture rounds and was bought by Amazon in 2018 for a reported ~$1B+. Heavy fundraising means an early 10% stake would have been diluted a lot, so we assume you keep about 30% of your original stake.
